children: Malaysia's fiscal slippage risks will likely be contained, despite recent cost-of-living relief measures that have raised concerns over election related fiscal populism, Citi analyst Wei Zheng Kit says in a note. Fuel subsidy increases are likely to be limited by tighter subsidy eligibility checks and low usage among eligible recipients. Stronger-than-budget revenue growth, higher oil prices and a potentially larger Petronas dividend should help offset higher spending, he says. The measures should help cap inflation risks following a lower-than-expected July CPI reading of 1.8% on year, he notes. Also, given an expected slowdown in 2H GDP growth and moderate consumption, Bank Negara may remain on hold in September and throughout 2027, but the risks are tilted toward a backloaded 25 bps hike, he adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
